thread:
Maria G: IncidentBot just paged for `pd-inference-agg-latency` on prod-east. sawtooth spike in 95th pct. Anyone oncall?
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident 12345 triggered for service 'inference-runtime' — urgency: high. Initial alert: 95th latency > 750ms over 3m. PagerDuty notified primary oncall.
Kevin L: oncall here, grabbing it. quick check of dashboards now.
Maria G: TY. customer-facing proxy error rate looks fine from quick glance but latency is high on some routes.
Kevin L: running `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep prod-east` — see a couple nodes with 70% GPU mem, but not OOM.
Olivia R: tagging in perf: maybe it's KV cache churn. saw repeating kv_warmup logs.
Kevin L: grabbing recent logs from runtime:```
[2026-03-15T09:03:12Z] kv_cache: evict prefix id=0x4f size=128
[2026-03-15T09:03:12Z] request: seq=1 len=512 model=redwood-7b q8
[2026-03-15T09:03:13Z] runtime: batch size=1 latency=860ms
```
Sam T: hmm that pattern looks like a cold/uncached tail for some customers causing sustained 95th.
Kevin L: I can silence the noisy PagerDuty rule for the 95th short-term to avoid paging while we investigate. Anyone object?
Maria G: go ahead, but annotate the incident. customers ok for now?
Olivia R: checked response codes for top 5 customers hitting that model — no errors, just slow. Risk low.
Kevin L: silencing rule `inference.95th.latency.alert` for 15m now. `pd silence add --service inference-runtime --duration 15m --reason "investigating sawtooth latency"`
IncidentBot: PagerDuty silence created for service 'inference-runtime' (15m) by Kevin L.
Sam T: while silenced I'm going to rotate a few worker pools to rebalance KV hot shards. rolling restart small batch.
Kevin L: command: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-worker -n prod-east --selector=pool=hot-shard-a` (batch=3)
Maria G: watching metrics — latency dropping on those pods after restart. nice.
Olivia R: still seeing a short spike every ~40s — looks like a synthetic canary bot pinging wide seq lengths, causing cache churn.
Sam T: I can patch the router to tag canary requests to a canary model variant to avoid pushing the real hash. small config change: `route: if header X-Canary==1 -> model=redwood-7b-canary`
Kevin L: applied patch to router config, reloaded.
IncidentBot: PagerDuty alert 12345 has been resolved automatically (no further alerts observed).
PagerDuty: Incident 12345 resolved — auto-resolved after 12m.
Maria G: closing the loop: root cause = synthetic canary/healthcheck traffic with unusually long seqs causing repeated KV cache eviction (sawtooth), which temporarily pushed 95th above threshold. No customer errors observed.
Olivia R: followups: add canary header, tune KV eviction threshold, and adjust alert to require sustained >5m to page.
Kevin L: filed a follow-up ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2048 — includes logs and config changes.
Sam T: thanks all — marking as no-customer-impact in incident doc.
Maria G: nice rapid mitigation. note for runbook: consider short silences for noisy transient 95th spikes. :thumbsup:
Kevin L: ack, adding to runbook and linking infra diff.
Maria G: last check — metrics stable. I'll update stakeholders.
Olivia R: thanks — good catch on canary behavior.
Kevin L: removing silence now so normal alerts resume.
IncidentBot: PagerDuty silence for 'inference-runtime' ended (auto).
